takeaway: The anterior mediastinum lies behind the sternum and in front of the great vessels. It contains the thymus, lymph nodes, fat and vessels.

question.text: Which of the following structures is located in the anterior mediastinum?

lines.text: The anterior mediastinum is the space just behind the sternum.
Right here, the thymus gland sits in front.
Behind it are the great vessels, which mark the back border of this compartment.
Besides the thymus, it holds lymph nodes, fat and vessels.
The oesophagus and trachea wait in other rooms, so they are not anterior.
Anterior mediastinal masses are classically thymic, substernal thyroid goitre, teratoma and other germ cell tumours, or lymphoma.
So remember: behind the sternum, think thymus.
